content: The Comprehensive Medical Evaluation and Assessment of Comorbidities, as outlined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), emphasizes the importance of a collaborative care model. This model, known as the Chronic Care Model (CCM), prioritizes a person-centered, team-based approach to healthcare. It necessitates robust collaboration between patients and healthcare providers to ensure optimal care delivery. Within the framework of the CCM, the focus is on creating a proactive healthcare environment. This approach encourages patients to actively participate in the development and execution of their care plans. The model underscores the importance of shared responsibility and accountability for health outcomes, empowering individuals with diabetes to take an active role in managing their condition in partnership with their healthcare team. By fostering a supportive environment, the CCM enables patients to establish and achieve personalized health goals. These goals are tailored to align with the patient’s unique lifestyle, preferences, and values, ensuring that care is both effective and meaningful to the individual.
